title: Explorar a hierarquia taxonômica
text: Aqui apresentamos um guia prático para a função funga_get_children_taxa() do pacote fungaR. Ela recupera todos os táxons filhos — espécies, subespécies, variedades e assim por diante — abaixo de um nome e nível taxonômico especificados, o que é útil para obter todas as espécies de um gênero, todos os gêneros de uma ordem, e outras travessias de hierarquia semelhantes.

title: Explorar a hierarquia taxonômica
text:
Visão Geral da Função
A funga_get_children_taxa() primeiro localiza o táxon pai na lista de espécies da Flora e Funga do Brasil (FFB), e então retorna todo táxon cuja linhagem inclua o ID de táxon desse pai. Os fungos são classificados na FFB por Divisão (equivalente a filo, ex.: Ascomycota, Basidiomycota) em vez de Classe, e a FFB não registra um táxon autônomo de nível família para fungos — rank = "family" continua funcionando, mas é comparado diretamente com a coluna de classificação family dos registros de gênero/espécie, em vez de percorrer uma linha de nível família.

title: Explorar a hierarquia taxonômica
text:
Argumentos







Argumento
Descrição




taxon_name
Caractere. Nome científico a buscar (ex.: "Trichoderma", "Xylariaceae", "Agaricales").


rank
Caractere. Nível taxonômico de taxon_name: "division", "order", "family", "genus", ou "species". Padrão "genus".


child_rank
Caractere ou NULL. Nível(is) a retornar como filhos. NULL (padrão) retorna todos os níveis descendentes; um único nível (ex.: "species") restringe o resultado apenas a esse nível. Solicitar child_rank = "family" a partir de uma divisão/ordem retorna um resumo derivado (nome da família, ordem e contagem de gêneros) em vez de linhas reais da FFB, já que estas não existem para fungos.


include_synonyms
Lógico. Se TRUE, inclui nomes sinônimos além dos aceitos. Padrão FALSE.


version
Versão do conjunto de dados da FFB a usar. Padrão "latest".


rm_funga_database
Se TRUE, exclui o banco de dados em cache após a busca. O padrão FALSE é recomendado para uso repetido.


verbose
Lógico. Se TRUE (padrão), imprime mensagens de progresso.

title: Explorar a hierarquia taxonômica
section: Obter todas as espécies de um gênero
text:
Obter todas as espécies de um gênero
library(fungaR)

species <- funga_get_children_taxa(taxon_name = "Trichoderma",
                                   rank = "genus",
                                   child_rank = "species")

title: Explorar a hierarquia taxonômica
section: Obter todos os descendentes de um gênero
text:

Espécies, subespécies e variedades juntas:
all_descendants <- funga_get_children_taxa(taxon_name = "Trichoderma",
                                           rank = "genus",
                                           child_rank = NULL)

title: Explorar a hierarquia taxonômica
section: Obter todos os gêneros de uma família, incluindo sinônimos
text:
Obter todos os gêneros de uma família, incluindo sinônimos
Comparado via a coluna de classificação family, já que a FFB não tem linha de nível família para fungos:
genera <- funga_get_children_taxa(taxon_name = "Xylariaceae",
                                  rank = "family",
                                  child_rank = "genus",
                                  include_synonyms = TRUE)

section: Obter todos os gêneros de uma ordem
text:
Obter todos os gêneros de uma ordem
genera_in_order <- funga_get_children_taxa(taxon_name = "Agaricales",
                                            rank = "order",
                                            child_rank = "genus")

title: Explorar a hierarquia taxonômica
text:
Dicas Adicionais

Defina child_rank = NULL quando quiser um panorama completo da diversidade de um grupo, incluindo táxons infraespecíficos; defina um único nível (ex.: "species") quando precisar especificamente de uma lista de espécies para uso posterior.
rank deve descrever corretamente taxon_name (ex.: não passe um nome de gênero com rank = "order") — a função busca o pai combinando os dois.
Combine com funga_records() quando precisar de filtros geográficos ou de atributos além da travessia de hierarquia (ex.: todas as espécies de um gênero que também sejam endêmicas de um determinado estado).

title: Verificar as versões disponíveis da FFB
text:
Aqui apresentamos um guia prático para a função funga_version() do pacote fungaR. Essa função recupera metadados sobre as versões do conjunto de dados da lista de espécies Flora e Funga do Brasil (FFB) atualmente publicadas no portal de dados IPT da FFB, hospedado pelo Jardim Botânico do Rio de Janeiro.
Como a FFB é uma lista de espécies viva, continuamente atualizada à medida que taxonomistas revisam e adicionam nomes, cada publicação do conjunto de dados é versionada. Verificar quais versões existem — e qual é a atual — costuma ser o primeiro passo antes de baixar, analisar ou filtrar dados da FFB, pois permite fixar sua análise em uma versão específica e citável.
crumbs: Verificar versões do conjunto de dados
Verificar as versões disponíveis da FFB

title: Verificar as versões disponíveis da FFB
text:
Visão Geral da Função
A funga_version() não recebe argumentos: ela simplesmente consulta os metadados do IPT da FFB e retorna um data frame resumindo cada versão publicada.

Coluna
Descrição

Número da versão da publicação do conjunto de dados.


Published_on
Data/hora da publicação do conjunto de dados.


Records
Número de registros incluídos na publicação.


URL
Link direto para a versão do conjunto de dados no portal IPT.


Latest
Lógico. TRUE para a linha correspondente à versão mais recentemente publicada.

title: Verificar as versões disponíveis da FFB
text:
Dicas Adicionais

As funções funga_download(), funga_parse(), e todas as demais construídas sobre elas (funga_records(), funga_search(), funga_match(), funga_get_children_taxa()), usam version = "latest" por padrão. Você só precisa chamar funga_version() diretamente quando quiser fixar uma análise em uma versão específica e mais antiga, por motivos de reprodutibilidade.
Informe uma string de versão específica da coluna Version (ex.: funga_download(version = versions_df$Version[1])) para trabalhar com essa versão exata em vez da atual.
A coluna Records é uma forma rápida de verificar se um download foi concluído corretamente: o número de linhas analisadas deve estar na mesma ordem de grandeza.

Visão Geral da Função

title: fungaR
text:
Flora e Funga do Brasil
Brazil harbors one of the richest fungal diversities in the world, spanning lichenized and non-lichenized fungi across every biome in the country. Assembling a complete, continuously updated checklist of this diversity has been a decades-long collaborative effort involving hundreds of taxonomists and mycologists across the country.
The project began in 2008 as the Lista de Espécies da Flora do Brasil, a first attempt to compile a national species checklist validated by specialists. It evolved into Flora do Brasil 2020, launched to meet Brazil’s commitments under the Global Strategy for Plant Conservation of the Convention on Biological Diversity, and — following the incorporation of fungi — into its current form, Flora e Funga do Brasil.
For each accepted fungal name, the checklist records nomenclatural status (accepted, synonym, or doubtful), taxonomic classification (Division, Order, Family, Genus — FFB does not use Class for Fungi), geographic distribution across Brazilian states and phytogeographic domains, endemism status, nutritional/ecological mode (e.g. saprobic, parasitic, lichenized, mycorrhizal), and substrate/host information. This structured, validated backbone underpins mycological research, conservation assessments, and biodiversity informatics across the country.
Data are published as versioned Darwin Core Archives through the FFB IPT Data Portal, hosted by the Rio de Janeiro Botanical Garden (JBRJ). fungaR reads directly from this portal, so every result reflects the checklist as curated by the taxonomist community at the time of the query.
If you are a taxonomist and wish to contribute new fungal names, updates, or corrections to Flora e Funga do Brasil, see the contribution guidelines on the platform itself, or contact the FFB coordination team at floraefungadobrasil@jbrj.gov.br. fungaR’s mycobank_gap(), spfungorum_gap(), and funga_distribution_gap() functions can help you find candidates worth submitting.

text:
Rede de Taxonomistas da Funga do Brasil
The Rede de Taxonomistas da Funga do Brasil (RTFB) brings together the specialists dedicated to documenting and validating data on fungi, lichens, and myxomycetes in FFB — the official reference base for government and society. The network grew naturally out of the long-standing effort of hundreds of people in Brazilian mycology to document fungal diversity, through initiatives such as the Flora e Funga do Brasil, the Herbário Virtual Reflora, the INCT Herbário Virtual da Flora e dos Fungos, the Catálogo da Vida do Brasil, the INCT Fungos do Brasil, and, more recently, the CNPq-funded Funga do Brasil Universal Project — all sharing the goal of strengthening collaboration between taxonomists and institutions.
RTFB’s purpose is to connect people, share knowledge, and promote the continuous updating of information on Brazil’s fungal diversity within FFB, the authoritative base for cataloguing fungal names. This work contributes directly to fungi being recognized in public policy, red lists, conservation plans, environmental regulations, and bioeconomy initiatives, driving the development of mycology in the country. The network’s own site serves as the main digital platform gathering information about its members, publications, news, and events, and connecting with other national and international initiatives.
Its main goals include:

Giving visibility to the network and bringing together taxonomist specialists on a platform with approved, verified profiles.
Facilitating access to publications and content related to fungal taxonomy.
Sharing news, events, and research results.
Providing data tools, including specimen counters in collections, identification status, and species assessed by CNCFlora/IUCN.
Integrating information with external databases, such as Flora e Funga do Brasil and IUCN, among others.

fungaR’s curation tools (mycobank_gap(), mycobank_records(), spfungorum_gap(), spfungorum_records(), and funga_distribution_gap()) are designed to support exactly this kind of collaborative curation work.

Here we present a practical guide to the mycobank_gap(), spfungorum_gap(), and funga_distribution_gap() functions of the fungaR package. Together, they support taxonomic experts curating and expanding Flora e Funga do Brasil (FFB)’s fungal coverage, by cross-checking global mycological and biodiversity repositories and flagging candidates worth a manual review.
Looking for MycoBank or Index Fungorum information on a taxon you already have in mind, rather than a comparison against FFB? See Retrieve records for a Brazilian taxon for mycobank_records()/spfungorum_records() instead.
All three functions write their results in three complementary forms: the returned data.frame, a downloadable .xlsx spreadsheet, and — by default (html_report = TRUE) — a self-contained HTML report with KPI counts, breakdown tables, and the full candidate/record table as a sortable, filterable DT widget with one-click copy/CSV/Excel download buttons, opened automatically in your browser in interactive sessions (open_report = interactive()).

title: Find species and state records missing from FFB
section: mycobank_gap(): find MycoBank species with Brazil evidence missing from FFB
text:
mycobank_gap(): find MycoBank species with Brazil evidence missing from FFB
Given a genus or order, mycobank_gap() cross-checks MycoBank’s global name database against the current FFB checklist. This is not a general diff of the two databases: by default, only species-level MycoBank names that MycoBank’s own locality data already places in Brazil — but that are still missing from FFB — are returned, so taxonomic experts get a shortlist of genuinely plausible new national records rather than every unrelated MycoBank name in the genus/order.
MycoBank has no public search API suited to bulk automation, so rather than scraping its live, JavaScript-driven search interface, the function downloads and caches MycoBank’s own bulk name export (MBList.zip, refreshed regularly by MycoBank), then filters it down to the requested genus or order using MycoBank’s Classification column. Names are compared against FFB by their currently accepted MycoBank name (not the raw name itself), so an obscure historical synonym of a species FFB already lists under a different name is not flagged as missing.
Determining Brazil evidence requires visiting each missing candidate’s own MycoBank name page (check_locality = TRUE, the default, via chromote, a headless-Chrome driver — MycoBank’s name pages are a JavaScript app with no static HTML fallback) to read the type specimen’s reported “Location details”, along with several other fields only available on that individual page: substrate/host, etymology, name type (e.g. Basionym/Combination), the type specimen voucher itself, its collector, and the original-publication (protolog) citation — beyond what MycoBank’s bulk export alone provides. When require_brazil_evidence = TRUE (the default), the result is then filtered down to only the candidates whose locality mentions Brazil; set it to FALSE to instead get every MycoBank name missing from FFB regardless of locality, with the evidence columns alongside for manual review. This intentionally does not cross-check GBIF/speciesLink here — see funga_distribution_gap() below for that.
A candidate counts as “already in FFB” if either its raw MycoBank name or its MycoBank currently accepted name matches an FFB species — not the current name alone — because MycoBank and FFB sometimes disagree on which genus a name currently belongs to.

Arguments







Argument
Description




taxon
Character. A single genus or order name (e.g. "Trichoderma" or "Xylariales").


rank
"genus" (default) or "order".


check_locality
If TRUE (default), each candidate’s own MycoBank name page is visited to read its reported locality/substrate. Requires the chromote package and a local Chrome/Chromium install; skipped with a message if unavailable.


require_brazil_evidence
If TRUE (default), the returned table is filtered to only candidates whose MycoBank locality mentions Brazil. Set FALSE to return every missing name regardless of locality. Only meaningful when check_locality = TRUE.


max_check
Safety cap on how many candidates are sent through the (one-page-load-per-name) locality check. Default 200.


version
FFB dataset version to compare against. Defaults to "latest".


mycobank_dir
Local directory used to cache the downloaded MycoBank export (~140MB). Defaults to "mycobank_download".


save
If TRUE (default), saves the result as an .xlsx spreadsheet.


html_report
If TRUE (default), also writes the interactive HTML report described above.





Value
A data frame, one row per MycoBank species-level name missing from FFB and, by default, with a Brazilian MycoBank locality, with its MycoBank number, author, year, name status, classification, current name, full synonymy text, original MycoBank URL (rendered as a clickable link in the HTML report), and — when check_locality = TRUE — several fields scraped from the name’s own MycoBank page: MycoBank_Locality, MycoBank_Substrate, MycoBank_Etymology, MycoBank_Name_Type, MycoBank_Type_Specimen, MycoBank_Collector, MycoBank_Protolog, and a MycoBank_Brazil_Evidence flag — ready for a taxonomist’s manual review.


Example
library(fungaR)

# MycoBank species in genus Trichoderma with a Brazilian MycoBank locality
# that are still missing from FFB
gap <- mycobank_gap(taxon = "Trichoderma", rank = "genus")

# Every MycoBank name missing from FFB regardless of locality, for manual review
gap_all <- mycobank_gap(taxon = "Trichoderma", rank = "genus",
                        require_brazil_evidence = FALSE)

# Faster, without the per-candidate locality check (no Brazil filtering possible)
gap_fast <- mycobank_gap(taxon = "Trichoderma", rank = "genus",
                         check_locality = FALSE)

title: Find species and state records missing from FFB
section: spfungorum_gap(): find Index Fungorum species with Brazil evidence missing from FFB
text:
spfungorum_gap(): find Index Fungorum species with Brazil evidence missing from FFB
Given a genus, spfungorum_gap() cross-checks Species Fungorum (Index Fungorum, Kew) against the current FFB checklist — the same “not a general diff” philosophy as mycobank_gap(), but sourced from Index Fungorum’s own reported locality instead of MycoBank’s.
Unlike MycoBank, Index Fungorum publishes a public, documented web service (fungus.asmx, a plain HTTP GET/XML API — no SOAP client or headless browser needed) that already returns every matching name’s own reported locality and host in a single request per genus. Index Fungorum’s LOCATION field very often names a Brazilian state directly (e.g. "Pernambuco") rather than the country itself, so the Brazil-evidence check covers the country name and every Brazilian state (matched as whole words, so e.g. “Paraguay” is never mistaken for the state “Pará”), not just the literal word “Brazil”. As with mycobank_gap(), a candidate counts as “already in FFB” if either its raw Index Fungorum name or its currently accepted name matches an FFB species.
By default (fetch_details = TRUE), each missing candidate’s own Species Fungorum page is also visited — a fast, plain HTTP request, no headless browser needed — to read the journal it was published in, the full formatted citation, the basionym/typification details, and the Index Fungorum LSID, and to correct Current_name with the freshly-scraped value whenever the bulk search response’s own (occasionally stale) field differs.

Arguments







Argument
Description




taxon
Character. A single genus name (e.g. "Phellinotus"). Index Fungorum’s web service has no operation for searching by higher classification, so order-level searches are not supported.


require_brazil_evidence
If TRUE (default), the returned table is filtered to only candidates whose Index Fungorum location mentions Brazil. Set FALSE to return every missing name regardless of locality.


fetch_details
If TRUE (default), visits each missing candidate’s own Species Fungorum page for its journal, full citation, basionym/typification details, and LSID, and to refresh Current_name. Set FALSE to skip this and use only the bulk search response’s own fields.


max_number
Maximum number of matching names requested from the web service in a single call. Default 1000, generous for any genus.


version
FFB dataset version to compare against. Defaults to "latest".


save
If TRUE (default), saves the result as an .xlsx spreadsheet.


html_report
If TRUE (default), also writes the interactive HTML report described above.





Value
A data frame, one row per Index Fungorum species-level name missing from FFB and, by default, with a Brazilian reported locality, with its Fungorum number, author, specific epithet, year, name status, current name, volume/part/page, publishing authors, original Species Fungorum URL (rendered as a clickable link in the HTML report), Fungorum_Location, Fungorum_Host, a Fungorum_Brazil_Evidence flag, and — when fetch_details = TRUE — Fungorum_Journal, Fungorum_Citation, Fungorum_Basionym, Fungorum_Current_Name_Citation, and Fungorum_LSID.


Example
library(fungaR)

# Index Fungorum species in genus Phellinotus with a Brazilian reported
# locality that are still missing from FFB
gap <- spfungorum_gap(taxon = "Phellinotus")

# Every Index Fungorum name missing from FFB regardless of locality, for manual review
gap_all <- spfungorum_gap(taxon = "Phellinotus", require_brazil_evidence = FALSE)

# Faster, without the per-candidate page visit
gap_fast <- spfungorum_gap(taxon = "Phellinotus", fetch_details = FALSE)

section: funga_distribution_gap(): find candidate new state records
text:
funga_distribution_gap(): find candidate new state records
Given a fungal genus or species, funga_distribution_gap() checks GBIF, speciesLink, and the Reflora Virtual Herbarium (via the refloraR package) for specimen evidence in Brazilian states that are not currently listed in FFB’s official distribution for that taxon — flagging candidate new state records.
Its HTML report goes one step further than the state-level summary: it also lists the actual individual occurrence records (not aggregated) found in the new-state-record candidate states, each linking directly to that record’s own page on GBIF or Reflora — exactly the evidence a taxonomist needs to verify the candidate.

Arguments







Argument
Description




taxon
Character. A single genus or species name (e.g. "Trichoderma harzianum").


state
Optional character vector restricting the check to specific states. NULL (default) checks all states with any evidence.


sources
Which sources to query: any of "gbif", "speciesLink", "reflora". Defaults to all three.


version
FFB dataset version to compare against. Defaults to "latest".


save
If TRUE (default), saves the result as an .xlsx spreadsheet.


html_report
If TRUE (default), also writes the interactive HTML report, including the individual-records table.





Value
A data frame, one row per Brazilian state with any occurrence evidence, flagging New_state_record_candidate = TRUE whenever a state has external evidence but is not in FFB’s official distribution.


Example
library(fungaR)

gap <- funga_distribution_gap(taxon = "Trichoderma harzianum")

# Restrict the check to two states, using only GBIF
gap_ba_pe <- funga_distribution_gap(taxon = "Trichoderma harzianum",
                                    state = c("Bahia", "Pernambuco"),
                                    sources = "gbif")

title: Find species and state records missing from FFB
text:
Additional Tips

speciesLink’s public API has, at the time of writing, a known SSL/endpoint reliability issue; funga_distribution_gap() treats speciesLink evidence as strictly best-effort and falls back gracefully to GBIF (and Reflora) when it is unreachable.
Install the refloraR package to include Reflora specimen evidence in funga_distribution_gap(); without it, that source is skipped with a message.
Install the chromote package (and have a local Chrome/Chromium install) to include the MycoBank locality check in mycobank_gap(); without it, that step (and the Brazil-evidence filtering that depends on it) is skipped with a message, and every missing name is returned unfiltered. spfungorum_gap() needs no such extra dependency.
Combine with funga_get_children_taxa() to build the candidate genus list you want to check against MycoBank or Index Fungorum.
mycobank_gap(), for larger genera or orders, can take a while when the per-candidate locality checks are enabled — start with check_locality = FALSE to size up how many candidates exist before running the full Brazil-evidence check. spfungorum_gap()’s Brazil-evidence filtering is always a single request regardless of genus size, but fetch_details = TRUE (the default) adds one fast plain-HTTP request per missing candidate for the journal/citation/basionym/LSID fields — set fetch_details = FALSE to skip that for very large result sets.

title: Resolve your own species names
text: Here we present a practical guide to the funga_search() and funga_match() functions of the fungaR package. Unlike funga_records(), which browses the checklist itself, these two functions take a list of names you already have — from your own herbarium, field survey, or collaborator — and resolve them against the Flora e Funga do Brasil (FFB) checklist.

title: Resolve your own species names
section: funga_search(): resolve a single name list
text:
funga_search(): resolve a single name list
funga_search() matches each name in a character vector against the FFB checklist. It tries an exact match first; if none is found, it falls back to a fuzzy (generalized Levenshtein-distance) match, which is what catches typos and minor spelling variants. When several checklist entries could match, the one classified "NOME_ACEITO" (accepted) is preferred, so synonyms are automatically resolved to their accepted name.

Arguments







Argument
Description




splist
Character vector of fungal names to search.


version
FFB dataset version to use. Defaults to "latest".


max_distance
Maximum edit distance allowed for a fuzzy match — an integer number of edits, or a fraction of name length (e.g. 0.2 allows roughly 1 edit per 5 characters). Default 0.2.


show_correct
If TRUE, appends a Correct column flagging exact (TRUE) vs. fuzzy (FALSE) matches.


genus_fuzzy
If FALSE (default), the genus must match exactly and only the epithet is fuzzily matched — considerably faster for large lists.


progress_bar
If TRUE, shows a progress bar.


rm_funga_database
If TRUE, deletes the cached database after searching. Default FALSE is recommended for repeated use.





Examples
library(fungaR)

# A single accepted name
funga_search("Trichoderma harzianum")

# A misspelled epithet, flagging exact vs. fuzzy matches
funga_search("Trichoderma harzianun", max_distance = 0.2, show_correct = TRUE)

# A synonym - resolves to the accepted name automatically
funga_search("Xylaria cornuta")

# A whole list at once
splist <- c("Trichoderma harzianum", "Xylaria polymorpha", "Trichoderma viride")
funga_search(splist, show_correct = TRUE, progress_bar = TRUE)

title: Resolve your own species names
section: funga_match(): compare two independent name lists
text:
funga_match(): compare two independent name lists
funga_match() searches two name lists independently with funga_search(), then aligns entries from both lists that resolve to the same accepted taxon — even when one or both sides used a synonym. This is useful for checking your species list against a collaborator’s, or reconciling two datasets that used different nomenclature.

Arguments







Argument
Description




splist1, splist2
Character vectors — the reference list and the list to match against it.


include_all
If TRUE (default), names found only in splist2 are appended to the result.


identify_dups
If TRUE (default), flags rows where two input names are synonyms of the same accepted taxon.


show_correct, genus_fuzzy, max_distance, version, rm_funga_database, progress_bar
Same meaning as in funga_search().





Example
splist1 <- c("Trichoderma harzianum", "Xylaria polymorpha", "Trichoderma viride")
splist2 <- c("Xylaria polymorpha var. minor", "Trichoderma viride", "Xylaria cornuta")

result <- funga_match(splist1, splist2, include_all = TRUE)

# Re-order splist2 to align with splist1
splist2[result$Match.Position.2to1]

title: Resolve your own species names
text:
Additional Tips

Keep rm_funga_database = FALSE (the default) across a session: the first funga_search()/funga_match() call downloads and parses the FFB dataset, and every subsequent call reuses that cache — repeated searches become nearly instant.
Use show_correct = TRUE when auditing a name list, so you can review every fuzzy match manually rather than trusting it blindly.
funga_match()’s Duplicated.Output.Position column is useful for spotting when two of your own names turn out to be synonyms of each other.

title: Parse FFB Darwin Core Archives
text: Here we present a practical guide to the funga_parse() function of the fungaR package. This function reads and organizes locally downloaded Darwin Core Archive (DwC-A) datasets from Flora e Funga do Brasil (FFB), turning the raw archive files into a clean, ready-to-use list of tables. It is the second step in the workflow, after funga_download().

title: Parse FFB Darwin Core Archives
Parse FFB Darwin Core Archives
text:
Arguments







Argument
Description




path
Character. Path to the local directory where the versioned FFB DwC-A folders were downloaded (usually created by funga_download()).


version
Character. "latest" parses the most recent downloaded version; "all" parses every downloaded version; a version string or vector parses specific versions.


verbose
Logical. If TRUE (default), prints informative progress messages.

title: Parse FFB Darwin Core Archives
text:
Output structure
funga_parse() returns a named list, one element per versioned folder (e.g. "dwca_ffb_v393_418"), each containing:

$meta: metadata describing the dataset structure.
$data: a nested list of parsed Darwin Core tables, including taxon.txt (with the new taxonName field), distribution.txt (with endemism and phytogeographicDomain columns), and speciesprofile.txt (with lifeForm, habitat, and vegetationType columns).

title: Parse FFB Darwin Core Archives
text:
Parse the latest downloaded version
library(fungaR)

# Step 1 - download (skip if already downloaded)
funga_download(version = "latest", dir = "funga_download")

# Step 2 - parse (works offline once downloaded)
dwca <- funga_parse(path = "funga_download", version = "latest")

# Step 3 - explore the parsed structure
names(dwca)
names(dwca[["dwca_ffb_v393_418"]][["data"]])

title: Parse FFB Darwin Core Archives
text:
Access individual tables
taxon_data        <- dwca[["dwca_ffb_v393_418"]][["data"]][["taxon.txt"]]
distribution_data <- dwca[["dwca_ffb_v393_418"]][["data"]][["distribution.txt"]]
profile_data       <- dwca[["dwca_ffb_v393_418"]][["data"]][["speciesprofile.txt"]]

title: Parse FFB Darwin Core Archives
text:
Additional Tips

You rarely need to call funga_parse() directly: funga_records() and the name-resolution functions call it automatically and reuse the cached, parsed result on repeated calls.
Because parsing works offline, it is a good way to inspect the raw structure of a dataset version without re-downloading it.
The generated taxonName field is the same clean binomial used internally by funga_search() for name matching, so it is a reliable join key if you need to merge FFB data with your own tables.

title: Frequently Asked Questions
text:
What is Flora e Funga do Brasil?
Flora e Funga do Brasil (FFB) is the taxonomic checklist that documents Brazil’s plant, algal, and fungal diversity — the richest in the world. Maintained by the Rio de Janeiro Botanical Garden and curated collaboratively by hundreds of taxonomists and mycologists, it records accepted names, synonyms, taxonomic classification, geographic distribution, endemism, nutritional/ecological mode, and substrate/host information for every documented fungal species.


What can I use fungaR for?
The fungaR package lets researchers and taxonomists download, parse, filter, and explore the fungal portion of the Flora e Funga do Brasil checklist directly from R. You can browse the checklist by taxonomic, geographic, or trait-based criteria, resolve your own species name lists against it (with fuzzy matching for typos), explore the taxonomic hierarchy, and cross-check MycoBank and Brazilian occurrence repositories to curate new species and state records for contribution back to FFB.


Do I need a list of species names to use fungaR?
No. funga_records() lets you browse and filter the FFB fungal checklist directly (e.g. all accepted species in a family, or all endemics in a given state) without providing any input names. If you already have your own species list — from a fungarium, field survey, or collaborator — funga_search() and funga_match() resolve those names against the checklist instead, with exact matching first and fuzzy (Levenshtein-distance) matching as a fallback for typos.


Does fungaR require an internet connection?
Only the first time you query a given dataset version, or MycoBank’s bulk name list. funga_download()/funga_parse() and mycobank_gap()/mycobank_records() fetch and cache their respective datasets locally, and every other function reuses that cache automatically, so repeated queries and offline analysis work without a new download. spfungorum_gap()/spfungorum_records() query Index Fungorum’s web service directly each time, since there is no bulk export to cache.


How do I install fungaR?
Visit the Get Started guide for installation instructions from GitHub.


Is fungaR free to use?
Yes. fungaR is open source, licensed under the MIT License.


Is this website available in Portuguese?
Yes. Every page has an EN/PT toggle in the navigation bar. Once you switch languages, the choice is remembered for the rest of your visit — you won’t need to switch again as you navigate between pages.


What output can fungaR generate?
fungaR returns tidy data frames (and, for funga_parse(), a structured list of DwC-A tables) ready for downstream analysis. funga_records() can save results directly to CSV, while mycobank_gap(), mycobank_records(), spfungorum_gap(), spfungorum_records(), and funga_distribution_gap() produce structured .xlsx spreadsheets — including each name’s original URL — designed for a taxonomist’s manual review.


Why does FFB use “Division” instead of “Class” for fungi, and no family-rank record?
FFB classifies fungi by Division (phylum-equivalent, e.g. Ascomycota, Basidiomycota) rather than Class, and does not register a standalone taxon record at family rank for Fungi — family is stored only as a classification column on genus/species records. funga_get_children_taxa() handles this automatically: rank = "family" still works, matched directly on that column instead of walking a family-rank row that does not exist.


What does the habitat field mean for fungi in funga_records()?
For fungi, FFB’s habitat field records the substrate/host the specimen was collected on (e.g. "Planta viva - raiz", "Tronco em decomposição", "Solo", "Outro fungo") rather than a plant growth habitat, since FFB does not publish a separate named host-taxon field. Use it to browse the checklist by substrate/host type.


Who is the developer of fungaR?
Development is led by JBRJ, with financial support from CNPq and FINEP. Main developer:

Domingos Cardoso (@DBOSlab)

View the code and contribute on GitHub: https://github.com/DBOSlab/fungaR


Why the name fungaR?
The name pairs “Funga” — for Flora e Funga do Brasil’s fungal component, the checklist it interfaces with — with the R programming language, reflecting the package’s goal of making the national fungal checklist directly and reproducibly accessible from R.


Where can I report bugs or request features?
Submit issues on GitHub: fungaR Issues.


Where can I ask questions and discuss fungaR?
Join our community via GitHub Discussions to ask questions, suggest ideas, or help others.


How does fungaR relate to Flora e Funga do Brasil?
The fungaR package is a programmatic interface to the fungal side of the Flora e Funga do Brasil IPT data portal: it downloads, parses, and queries the same checklist data published on the platform, and also helps taxonomic experts prepare new fungal names and records for contribution back to it.


Can I contribute new fungal names or records to Flora e Funga do Brasil?
Yes. fungaR includes mycobank_gap(), spfungorum_gap(), and funga_distribution_gap() specifically to help taxonomic experts find candidates worth submitting — cross-checking MycoBank’s and Index Fungorum’s global name databases, and Brazilian occurrence repositories (GBIF, speciesLink, REFLORA), against the current FFB checklist to flag species and state records that are plausibly Brazilian but still missing. If you already have a taxon in mind rather than needing an FFB comparison, mycobank_records()/spfungorum_records() retrieve everything those repositories have on record for it directly. To submit new names or corrections to the platform itself, see the contribution guidelines at floradobrasil.jbrj.gov.br/consulta or contact the FFB coordination team at floraefungadobrasil@jbrj.gov.br.

title: Download the FFB checklist
text: Here we present a practical guide to the funga_download() function of the fungaR package. This function downloads taxonomic and distributional records from the Flora e Funga do Brasil (FFB) platform in Darwin Core Archive (DwC-A) format, directly from the FFB IPT data portal.

title: Download the FFB checklist
text:
Function Overview
funga_download() retrieves one or more versions of the FFB dataset and saves each one to its own subdirectory on disk. It checks whether a requested version is already present locally and avoids re-downloading it unnecessarily, so it is safe to call repeatedly across a project.

title: Download the FFB checklist
text:
Arguments







Argument
Description




version
Character. "latest" (default) downloads the most recent release; "all" downloads every available version (large!); a version string or vector of version strings (e.g. "393.418") downloads specific releases. Use funga_version() to inspect valid version numbers first.


verbose
Logical. If TRUE (default), prints informative messages during download.


dir
Character. Local directory to save the downloaded files. Defaults to "funga_download". Each version is extracted into its own subdirectory.

title: Download the FFB checklist
text:
Download the latest dataset
library(fungaR)

funga_download(dir = "funga_download")

title: Download the FFB checklist
text:
Download a specific version
Use funga_version() first to find a valid version string:
versions_df <- funga_version()

funga_download(version = versions_df$Version[1], dir = "funga_download")

title: Download the FFB checklist
text:
Download multiple versions
funga_download(version = c("393.418", "392.417"), dir = "funga_download")

title: Download the FFB checklist
text:
Download every available version
# Large download! Only needed for archival or cross-version comparisons.
funga_download(version = "all", dir = "funga_download")

title: Download the FFB checklist
text:
Additional Tips

You rarely need to call funga_download() directly: funga_records(), funga_search(), funga_match(), and funga_get_children_taxa() all download and cache the dataset automatically the first time you call them.
If no internet connection is available, funga_download() automatically falls back to a previously downloaded local copy, if one exists in dir.
Keep the downloaded folder (the default rm_funga_database = FALSE behavior in downstream functions) so that repeated analyses reuse the cache instead of re-downloading the archive every time.

title: Check available FFB dataset versions
text:
Here we present a practical guide to the funga_version() function of the fungaR package. This function retrieves metadata about the dataset versions of the Flora e Funga do Brasil (FFB) checklist currently published on the FFB IPT data portal, hosted by the Rio de Janeiro Botanical Garden.
Because FFB is a living checklist, continuously updated as taxonomists review and add names, every dataset release is versioned. Checking which versions exist — and which one is current — is normally the first step before downloading, parsing, or filtering FFB data, since it lets you pin your analysis to a specific, citable release.

title: Check available FFB dataset versions
text:
Function Overview
funga_version() takes no arguments: it simply queries the FFB IPT metadata and returns a data frame summarizing every published version.

title: Check available FFB dataset versions
text:
Output columns







Column
Description




Version
Version number of the dataset release.


Published_on
Timestamp of the dataset release.


Records
Number of records included in the release.


URL
Direct link to the dataset version on the IPT portal.


Latest
Logical. TRUE for the row corresponding to the most recently published version.

title: Check available FFB dataset versions
text:
List all available versions
library(fungaR)

versions_df <- funga_version()
head(versions_df)

title: Check available FFB dataset versions
text:
Identify the latest version
latest <- versions_df[versions_df$Latest == TRUE, ]
latest$Version

title: Check available FFB dataset versions
text:
Additional Tips

funga_download() and funga_parse(), and every function built on top of them (funga_records(), funga_search(), funga_match(), funga_get_children_taxa()), default to version = "latest". You only need funga_version() directly when you want to pin an analysis to a specific, older release for reproducibility.
Pass a specific version string from the Version column (e.g. funga_download(version = versions_df$Version[1])) to work with that exact release instead of the current one.
The Records column is a quick way to sanity-check that a download completed correctly: the number of parsed rows should be in the same order of magnitude.

title: Explore the taxonomic hierarchy
text: Here we present a practical guide to the funga_get_children_taxa() function of the fungaR package. It retrieves all child taxa — species, subspecies, varieties, and so on — below a given taxonomic name and rank, which is useful for getting every species in a genus, every genus in an order, and similar hierarchy traversals.

title: Explore the taxonomic hierarchy
text:
Function Overview
funga_get_children_taxa() first locates the parent taxon in the Flora e Funga do Brasil (FFB) checklist, then returns every taxon whose lineage includes that parent’s taxon ID. Fungi are classified in FFB by Division (phylum-equivalent, e.g. Ascomycota, Basidiomycota) rather than Class, and FFB does not register a standalone family-rank taxon record for Fungi — rank = "family" is still supported, but matched directly against the family classification column on genus/species records instead of walking a family-rank row.

title: Explore the taxonomic hierarchy
text:
Arguments







Argument
Description




taxon_name
Character. Scientific name to search for (e.g. "Trichoderma", "Xylariaceae", "Agaricales").


rank
Character. Taxonomic rank of taxon_name: "division", "order", "family", "genus", or "species". Default "genus".


child_rank
Character or NULL. Rank(s) to return as children. NULL (default) returns all descendant ranks; a single rank (e.g. "species") restricts the result to that rank only. Requesting child_rank = "family" from a division/order returns a derived summary (family name, order, and genus count) rather than real FFB rows, since none exist for Fungi.


include_synonyms
Logical. If TRUE, includes synonym names in addition to accepted ones. Default FALSE.


version
FFB dataset version to use. Defaults to "latest".


rm_funga_database
If TRUE, deletes the cached database after the search. Default FALSE is recommended for repeated use.


verbose
Logical. If TRUE (default), prints progress messages.

title: Explore the taxonomic hierarchy
section: Get all species in a genus
text:
Get all species in a genus
library(fungaR)

species <- funga_get_children_taxa(taxon_name = "Trichoderma",
                                   rank = "genus",
                                   child_rank = "species")

title: Explore the taxonomic hierarchy
section: Get every descendant of a genus
text:
Get every descendant of a genus
Species, subspecies, and varieties together:
all_descendants <- funga_get_children_taxa(taxon_name = "Trichoderma",
                                           rank = "genus",
                                           child_rank = NULL)

title: Explore the taxonomic hierarchy
section: Get all genera in a family, including synonyms
text:
Get all genera in a family, including synonyms
Matched via the family classification column, since FFB has no family-rank row for Fungi:
genera <- funga_get_children_taxa(taxon_name = "Xylariaceae",
                                  rank = "family",
                                  child_rank = "genus",
                                  include_synonyms = TRUE)

title: Explore the taxonomic hierarchy
section: Get all genera in an order
text:
Get all genera in an order
genera_in_order <- funga_get_children_taxa(taxon_name = "Agaricales",
                                            rank = "order",
                                            child_rank = "genus")

title: Explore the taxonomic hierarchy
text:
Additional Tips

Set child_rank = NULL when you want a complete picture of a group’s diversity, including infraspecific taxa; set it to a single rank (e.g. "species") when you specifically need a species-level checklist for downstream work.
rank must correctly describe taxon_name (e.g. don’t pass a genus name with rank = "order") — the function looks up the parent by matching both together.
Combine with funga_records() when you need geographic or trait filters in addition to hierarchy traversal (e.g. all species in a genus that are also endemic to a given state).

title: Filter and retrieve checklist records
text: Here we present a practical guide to the funga_records() function of the fungaR package. Unlike funga_search() and funga_match(), which resolve a list of names you already have against the checklist, funga_records() browses and filters the fungal side of the Flora e Funga do Brasil (FFB) checklist directly — no input name list required.

title: Filter and retrieve checklist records
text:
Function Overview
funga_records() downloads and parses the FFB dataset automatically (like funga_search(), reusing the local cache on repeated calls), then applies whichever combination of taxonomic, geographic, and trait-based filters you request. All filters are combined with a logical AND, and the result always has one row per matching taxon — appended with that taxon’s distribution and species-profile information (see Output columns below).

title: Filter and retrieve checklist records
text:
Arguments







Argument
Description




taxon
Character vector. One or more family, genus, or species names to filter by (e.g. c("Hymenochaetaceae", "Trichoderma", "Xylaria hypoxylon")).


taxonRank
Character vector. Taxonomic rank(s) to keep (e.g. "ESPECIE", "VARIEDADE", "SUBESPECIE", "FORMA", "GENERO", "ORDEM", "DIVISAO" — fungi are classified by Division/phylum rather than Class).


taxonomicStatus
Character vector. FFB taxonomic status: "NOME_ACEITO" (accepted), "SINONIMO" (synonym), or "NOME_DUVIDOSO" (doubtful).


state
Character vector. Brazilian state(s), full name or acronym, diacritics-insensitive (e.g. "Bahia" or "BA").


phytogeographicDomain
Character vector. Phytogeographic domain(s) (e.g. "Caatinga", "Mata Atlantica").


endemism
Logical. TRUE keeps only Brazilian endemics; FALSE keeps only non-endemics.


lifeForm, habitat, vegetationType
Character vectors. Nutritional/ecological mode (e.g. "Saprobio", "Liquenizado"), substrate/host (e.g. "Tronco em decomposicao", "Solo", "Outro fungo" — this is what habitat means for fungi, since FFB has no separate named host-taxon field) and vegetation type (e.g. "Cerrado (lato sensu)").


version
Character. FFB dataset version to use. Defaults to "latest".


rm_funga_database
Logical. If TRUE, deletes the downloaded database after the search. Default FALSE keeps it cached for faster repeated queries.


verbose
Logical. If TRUE (default), prints progress messages.


save
Logical. If TRUE, writes the filtered records to a CSV file.


dir, filename
Where and under what name to save the CSV when save = TRUE.

title: Filter and retrieve checklist records
text:
Output columns
Beyond the taxon table columns (taxonName, family, genus, taxonRank, taxonomicStatus, …), every result also carries the matching taxon’s distribution and species-profile information:








Column
Source
Notes




state
distribution table
Brazilian state(s) with occurrence records


phytogeographicDomain
distribution table
Phytogeographic domain(s)


endemism
distribution table
Endemism status as recorded by FFB


lifeForm
species profile table
Nutritional/ecological mode(s)


habitat
species profile table
Substrate/host record(s)


vegetationType
species profile table
Vegetation type(s)



A single taxon can have several distribution or species-profile records (e.g. occurring in multiple states, or recorded on multiple substrates). Rather than multiplying rows, funga_records() concatenates all distinct values for each of these columns with " | ", so the result always keeps exactly one row per taxon.

title: Filter and retrieve checklist records
text:
Browse a whole family
library(fungaR)

hymeno <- funga_records(taxon = "Hymenochaetaceae",
                        taxonomicStatus = "NOME_ACEITO")

title: Filter and retrieve checklist records
text:
Filter by state and endemism
bahia_endemics <- funga_records(state = "Bahia",
                                endemism = TRUE,
                                taxonomicStatus = "NOME_ACEITO")

title: Filter and retrieve checklist records
section: Filter by phytogeographic domain and nutritional mode
text:
Filter by phytogeographic domain and nutritional mode
caatinga_lichens <- funga_records(phytogeographicDomain = "Caatinga",
                                  lifeForm = "Liquenizado")

title: Filter and retrieve checklist records
text:
Filter by substrate/host
root_associates <- funga_records(habitat = "Planta viva - raiz")

title: Filter and retrieve checklist records
section: Save the result to a CSV file
text:
Save the result to a CSV file
funga_records(taxon = "Trichoderma",
             save = TRUE,
             dir = "funga_records",
             filename = "trichoderma_records")

title: Filter and retrieve checklist records
text:
Additional Tips

taxon is matched against the family, genus and taxonName columns automatically — a family name ending in "aceae", a single-word genus, or a multi-word species name are all detected and matched appropriately.
Combine multiple filters freely: they are always ANDed together, so funga_records(taxon = "Hymenochaetaceae", state = "Bahia", endemism = TRUE) returns Hymenochaetaceae species endemic to Bahia.
If you already have your own species list to resolve rather than browse the checklist by criteria, use funga_search() or funga_match() instead.

title: Retrieve records for a Brazilian taxon
text:
Here we present a practical guide to mycobank_records() and spfungorum_records(), two fungaR functions for retrieving nomenclatural information about a Brazilian fungal taxon from MycoBank and Species Fungorum (Index Fungorum, maintained by the Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew) respectively. Unlike mycobank_gap() and spfungorum_gap(), these are not comparisons against the Flora e Funga do Brasil (FFB) checklist — it doesn’t matter whether the taxon is already registered in FFB. They are straightforward retrieval tools: give either one a species or genus, and it returns everything that repository has on record for it, filtered by default to only the names placed in Brazil.
Both functions write their results in three complementary forms: the returned data.frame, a downloadable .xlsx spreadsheet, and — by default (html_report = TRUE) — a self-contained HTML report with KPI counts and the full record table as a sortable, filterable DT widget with one-click copy/CSV/Excel download buttons, opened automatically in your browser in interactive sessions (open_report = interactive()).

title: Retrieve records for a Brazilian taxon
section: When to use these instead of mycobank_gap()/spfungorum_gap()
text:
When to use these instead of mycobank_gap()/spfungorum_gap()

Use mycobank_records()/spfungorum_records() when you already have a taxon in mind — a single species, or every species in a genus — and want to see everything that repository knows about the Brazilian occurrence(s), regardless of FFB status.
Use mycobank_gap()/spfungorum_gap() when you want to find candidates FFB is missing — they add the FFB comparison step and only return names absent from the checklist.
crumbs: Retrieve records for a Brazilian taxon

title: Retrieve records for a Brazilian taxon
section: mycobank_records(): retrieve MycoBank records for a taxon
text:
mycobank_records(): retrieve MycoBank records for a taxon
MycoBank has no public search API suited to bulk automation, so rather than scraping its live, JavaScript-driven search interface, mycobank_records() downloads and caches MycoBank’s own bulk name export (MBList.zip, refreshed regularly by MycoBank, shared with mycobank_gap()’s cache), then filters it down to the requested species, genus, or order.
The bulk export carries no locality information, so determining Brazil evidence requires visiting each matching name’s own MycoBank page (check_locality = TRUE, the default, via chromote, a headless-Chrome driver — MycoBank’s name pages are a JavaScript app with no static HTML fallback) to read the type specimen’s reported “Location details”, along with several other fields only available on that individual page: substrate/host, etymology, name type (e.g. Basionym/Combination), the type specimen voucher itself, its collector, and the original-publication (protolog) citation. When require_brazil_evidence = TRUE (the default), the result is then filtered down to only the names whose locality mentions Brazil; set it to FALSE to instead get every matching MycoBank name regardless of locality, with the evidence columns alongside for manual review.

Arguments







Argument
Description




taxon
Character. A single species, genus, or order name (e.g. "Trichoderma harzianum", "Trichoderma", or "Xylariales").


rank
"species" (default), "genus", or "order".


check_locality
If TRUE (default), each matching name’s own MycoBank page is visited to read its reported locality/substrate. Requires the chromote package and a local Chrome/Chromium install; skipped with a message if unavailable.


require_brazil_evidence
If TRUE (default), the returned table is filtered to only names whose MycoBank locality mentions Brazil. Set FALSE to return every matching name regardless of locality. Only meaningful when check_locality = TRUE.


max_check
Safety cap on how many matching names are sent through the (one-page-load-per-name) locality check. Default 200.


mycobank_dir
Local directory used to cache the downloaded MycoBank export (~140MB). Defaults to "mycobank_download".


save
If TRUE (default), saves the result as an .xlsx spreadsheet.


html_report
If TRUE (default), also writes the interactive HTML report described above.





Value
A data frame, one row per matching MycoBank name and, by default, with a Brazilian MycoBank locality, with its MycoBank number, author, year, name status, classification, current name, full synonymy text, original MycoBank URL (rendered as a clickable link in the HTML report), and — when check_locality = TRUE — several fields scraped from the name’s own MycoBank page: MycoBank_Locality, MycoBank_Substrate, MycoBank_Etymology, MycoBank_Name_Type, MycoBank_Type_Specimen, MycoBank_Collector, MycoBank_Protolog, and a MycoBank_Brazil_Evidence flag.


Example
library(fungaR)

# All MycoBank information for a single species, only if MycoBank places it in Brazil
sp <- mycobank_records(taxon = "Trichoderma harzianum")

# Every MycoBank species-level name in genus Trichoderma with a Brazilian MycoBank locality
genus_records <- mycobank_records(taxon = "Trichoderma", rank = "genus")

# Every matching name regardless of locality, for manual review
all_records <- mycobank_records(taxon = "Trichoderma", rank = "genus",
                                require_brazil_evidence = FALSE)

# Faster, without the per-candidate locality check (no Brazil filtering possible)
fast_records <- mycobank_records(taxon = "Trichoderma", rank = "genus",
                                 check_locality = FALSE)
crumbs: Retrieve records for a Brazilian taxon

title: Retrieve records for a Brazilian taxon
section: spfungorum_records(): retrieve Index Fungorum records for a taxon
text:
spfungorum_records(): retrieve Index Fungorum records for a taxon
Species Fungorum/Index Fungorum has no bulk export, but it does publish a public, documented web service (fungus.asmx, a plain HTTP GET/XML API - no SOAP client, headless browser, or authentication required) that spfungorum_records() queries directly. A single request returns every name matching taxon, including, for many records, the type specimen’s own reported LOCATION and HOST.
Index Fungorum’s LOCATION field very often names a Brazilian state directly (e.g. "Pernambuco") rather than the country itself, so Fungorum_Brazil_Evidence checks the location against the country name and every Brazilian state name (with or without diacritics, and matched as whole words so e.g. “Paraguay” is never mistaken for the state “Pará”), not just the literal word “Brazil”.
By default (fetch_details = TRUE), each returned name’s own Species Fungorum page is also visited - a fast, plain HTTP request, no headless browser needed, unlike MycoBank - to read the journal it was published in, the full formatted citation, the basionym/typification details, and the Index Fungorum LSID. This also corrects Current_name: the bulk search response caches that field on the original name’s own row, which can go stale relative to the current name’s own record, so the freshly-scraped value is preferred whenever available.

Arguments







Argument
Description




taxon
Character. A single species or genus name (e.g. "Phellinotus neoaridus" or "Phellinotus").


rank
"species" (default) or "genus". Index Fungorum’s web service has no operation for searching by higher classification, so order-level searches are not supported.


require_brazil_evidence
If TRUE (default), the returned table is filtered to only names whose Index Fungorum location mentions Brazil. Set FALSE to return every matching name regardless of locality.


fetch_details
If TRUE (default), visits each name’s own Species Fungorum page for its journal, full citation, basionym/typification details, and LSID, and to refresh Current_name. Set FALSE to skip this and use only the bulk search response’s own fields.


max_number
Maximum number of matching names requested from the web service in a single call. Default 1000, generous for any genus.


save
If TRUE (default), saves the result as an .xlsx spreadsheet.


html_report
If TRUE (default), also writes the interactive HTML report described above.





Value
A data frame, one row per matching Index Fungorum name and, by default, with a Brazilian reported locality, with its Fungorum number, author, specific epithet, year, name status, current name, volume/part/page, publishing authors, original Species Fungorum URL (rendered as a clickable link in the HTML report), Fungorum_Location, Fungorum_Host, a Fungorum_Brazil_Evidence flag, and — when fetch_details = TRUE — Fungorum_Journal, Fungorum_Citation, Fungorum_Basionym, Fungorum_Current_Name_Citation, and Fungorum_LSID.


Example
library(fungaR)

# All Index Fungorum information for a single species, only if it reports a
# Brazilian locality
sp <- spfungorum_records(taxon = "Phellinotus neoaridus")

# Every Index Fungorum species-level name in genus Phellinotus with a
# Brazilian reported locality
genus_records <- spfungorum_records(taxon = "Phellinotus", rank = "genus")

# Every matching name regardless of locality, for manual review
all_records <- spfungorum_records(taxon = "Phellinotus", rank = "genus",
                                  require_brazil_evidence = FALSE)

# Faster, without the per-record page visit (journal/citation/basionym/LSID
# omitted, and Current_name uses the bulk response's value as-is)
fast_records <- spfungorum_records(taxon = "Phellinotus", rank = "genus",
                                   fetch_details = FALSE)
crumbs: Retrieve records for a Brazilian taxon

title: Retrieve records for a Brazilian taxon
text:
Additional Tips

Install the chromote package (and have a local Chrome/Chromium install) to include mycobank_records()’s locality check; without it, that step (and the Brazil-evidence filtering that depends on it) is skipped with a message, and every matching name is returned unfiltered. spfungorum_records() needs no such extra dependency for its Brazil-evidence check specifically - the country/state locality always comes back with the initial bulk request, regardless of fetch_details.
mycobank_dir is shared between mycobank_records() and mycobank_gap() - pointing both functions at the same directory avoids re-downloading MycoBank’s bulk export twice.
For larger genera, mycobank_records()’s per-candidate locality check can take a while - start with check_locality = FALSE to size up how many names match before running the full Brazil-evidence check. spfungorum_records()’s Brazil-evidence filtering is always a single request regardless of genus size, but fetch_details = TRUE (the default) adds one fast plain-HTTP request per returned name for the journal/citation/basionym/LSID fields - set fetch_details = FALSE to skip that for very large result sets.

title: About fungaR
text:
Overview
fungaR is an R package for accessing, analyzing, and curating fungal taxonomic and distributional data from the Flora e Funga do Brasil (FFB) platform, maintained by the Rio de Janeiro Botanical Garden. It offers a comprehensive interface to the FFB IPT data portal: downloading, parsing, filtering, and exploring versioned Darwin Core Archive (DwC-A) checklist data — from browsing by taxonomic, geographic, or trait criteria (including fungi-specific traits such as nutritional mode and substrate/host) to resolving your own species name lists against it.
Beyond data retrieval, fungaR also assists taxonomic experts contributing to FFB by cross-checking MycoBank, Species Fungorum (Index Fungorum), and Brazilian occurrence repositories — GBIF, speciesLink, and the Reflora Virtual Herbarium — to flag fungal species and state records that are plausibly Brazilian but still missing from the platform.

title: About fungaR
text:
Flora e Funga do Brasil
Brazil harbors one of the richest fungal diversities in the world. The checklist that documents it began in 2008 as the Lista de Espécies da Flora do Brasil, evolved into Flora do Brasil 2020 to meet Brazil’s Global Strategy for Plant Conservation commitments, and — after incorporating fungi — became Flora e Funga do Brasil.
For each accepted fungal name, FFB records nomenclatural status, taxonomic classification (Division, Order, Family, Genus), geographic distribution, endemism, nutritional/ecological mode, and substrate/host information — a validated taxonomic backbone assembled collaboratively by hundreds of taxonomists and mycologists, and published as versioned Darwin Core Archives.

title: About fungaR
section: Rede de Taxonomistas da Funga do Brasil
text:
Rede de Taxonomistas da Funga do Brasil
The Rede de Taxonomistas da Funga do Brasil (RTFB) is a network connecting the specialists who document and validate Brazil’s fungal, lichen, and myxomycete diversity in FFB. It grew out of decades of collaborative work across initiatives such as the Catálogo de Plantas e Fungos do Brasil and the INCT Herbário Virtual da Flora e dos Fungos, and now serves as a shared platform for its members, their publications, and community news. fungaR’s curation tools (mycobank_gap(), mycobank_records(), spfungorum_gap(), spfungorum_records(), and funga_distribution_gap()) are designed to support exactly this kind of collaborative curation work.

Author: Domingos Cardoso (@DBOSlab ORCID)

Features

Version tracking and offline-capable parsing of downloaded DwC-A datasets
Checklist filtering by taxonomic, geographic, and trait-based (including substrate/host) criteria
Exact and fuzzy (Levenshtein-distance) name resolution against the checklist

Cross-checking MycoBank, Index Fungorum, GBIF, speciesLink, and REFLORA to flag species and state records missing from FFB, or retrieving MycoBank/Index Fungorum records for a Brazilian taxon directly

title: Perguntas Frequentes
text:
O que é a Flora e Funga do Brasil?
A Flora e Funga do Brasil (FFB) é a lista de espécies taxonômica que documenta a diversidade de plantas, algas e fungos do Brasil — a mais rica do mundo. Mantida pelo Jardim Botânico do Rio de Janeiro e curada colaborativamente por centenas de taxonomistas e micologistas, ela registra nomes aceitos, sinônimos, classificação taxonômica, distribuição geográfica, endemismo, modo nutricional/ecológico, e informações de substrato/hospedeiro para cada espécie fúngica documentada.


Para que posso usar o fungaR?
O pacote fungaR permite que pesquisadores e taxonomistas baixem, analisem, filtrem, e explorem a porção fúngica da lista de espécies da Flora e Funga do Brasil diretamente a partir do R. Você pode navegar pela lista de espécies por critérios taxonômicos, geográficos, ou de atributos, resolver sua própria lista de nomes de espécies em relação a ela (com correspondência aproximada para erros de digitação), explorar a hierarquia taxonômica, e cruzar dados com o MycoBank, o Index Fungorum, e repositórios de ocorrência brasileiros para curar novas espécies e registros estaduais para contribuição de volta à FFB.


Preciso de uma lista de nomes de espécies para usar o fungaR?
Não. A função funga_records() permite navegar e filtrar a lista de espécies fúngicas da FFB diretamente (por exemplo, todas as espécies aceitas de uma família, ou todos os endemismos de um determinado estado) sem fornecer nenhum nome de entrada. Se você já tem sua própria lista de espécies — de um fungário, levantamento de campo, ou colaborador — as funções funga_search() e funga_match() resolvem esses nomes em relação à lista de espécies, com correspondência exata primeiro e correspondência aproximada (distância de Levenshtein) como alternativa para erros de digitação.


O fungaR requer conexão com a internet?
Apenas na primeira vez que você consultar uma determinada versão do conjunto de dados, ou a lista de nomes em lote do MycoBank. As funções funga_download()/funga_parse() e mycobank_gap()/mycobank_records() baixam e armazenam localmente seus respectivos conjuntos de dados, e todas as demais funções reutilizam esse cache automaticamente, de modo que consultas repetidas e análises offline funcionam sem um novo download. spfungorum_gap()/spfungorum_records() consultam o serviço web do Index Fungorum diretamente a cada vez, já que não há exportação em lote para armazenar em cache.


Como instalo o fungaR?
Visite o guia de Instalação para instruções de instalação a partir do GitHub.


O fungaR é gratuito?
Sim. fungaR é de código aberto, licenciado sob a Licença MIT.


Este site está disponível em português?
Sim. Toda página tem um alternador EN/PT na barra de navegação. Depois que você muda de idioma, a escolha é lembrada pelo restante da sua visita — você não precisará alternar novamente ao navegar entre páginas.


Quais saídas o fungaR pode gerar?
O fungaR retorna data frames organizados (e, no caso de funga_parse(), uma lista estruturada de tabelas DwC-A) prontos para análise. A função funga_records() pode salvar resultados diretamente em CSV, enquanto mycobank_gap(), mycobank_records(), spfungorum_gap(), spfungorum_records(), e funga_distribution_gap() produzem planilhas .xlsx estruturadas — incluindo a URL original de cada nome — projetadas para a revisão manual de um taxonomista.


Por que a FFB usa “Divisão” em vez de “Classe” para fungos, e não tem registro de nível família?
A FFB classifica fungos por Divisão (equivalente a filo, ex.: Ascomycota, Basidiomycota) em vez de Classe, e não registra um táxon autônomo de nível família para Fungi — família é armazenada apenas como uma coluna de classificação nos registros de gênero/espécie. A funga_get_children_taxa() trata isso automaticamente: rank = "family" continua funcionando, comparado diretamente com essa coluna em vez de percorrer uma linha de nível família que não existe.


O que o campo habitat significa para fungos em funga_records()?
Para fungos, o campo habitat da FFB registra o substrato/hospedeiro em que o espécime foi coletado (ex.: "Planta viva - raiz", "Tronco em decomposição", "Solo", "Outro fungo") em vez de um hábito de crescimento vegetal, já que a FFB não publica um campo de táxon-hospedeiro nomeado separadamente. Use-o para navegar a lista de espécies por tipo de substrato/hospedeiro.


Quem é o desenvolvedor do fungaR?
O desenvolvimento é liderado pelo JBRJ, com apoio financeiro do CNPq e da FINEP. Desenvolvedor principal:

Domingos Cardoso (@DBOSlab)

Veja o código e contribua no GitHub: https://github.com/DBOSlab/fungaR


Por que o nome fungaR?
O nome combina “Funga” — para o componente fúngico da Flora e Funga do Brasil, a lista de espécies com a qual o pacote interage — com a linguagem de programação R, refletindo o objetivo do pacote de tornar a lista nacional de fungos direta e reprodutivelmente acessível a partir do R.


Onde posso reportar bugs ou solicitar funcionalidades?
Envie issues no GitHub: fungaR Issues.


Onde posso fazer perguntas e discutir sobre o fungaR?
Participe da nossa comunidade nas Discussões do GitHub para fazer perguntas, sugerir ideias, ou ajudar outros usuários.


Como o fungaR se relaciona com a Flora e Funga do Brasil?
O pacote fungaR é uma interface programática para o lado fúngico do portal de dados IPT da Flora e Funga do Brasil: ele baixa, analisa, e consulta os mesmos dados da lista de espécies publicados na plataforma, e também ajuda especialistas taxonomistas a preparar novos nomes e registros fúngicos para contribuição de volta a ela.


Posso contribuir com novos nomes ou registros fúngicos para a Flora e Funga do Brasil?
Sim. O fungaR inclui mycobank_gap(), spfungorum_gap(), e funga_distribution_gap() especificamente para ajudar especialistas taxonomistas a encontrar candidatos que valem a pena submeter — cruzando as bases de nomes globais do MycoBank e do Index Fungorum, e repositórios de ocorrência brasileiros (GBIF, speciesLink, REFLORA), com a lista de espécies atual da FFB para sinalizar espécies e registros estaduais que são plausivelmente brasileiros mas ainda estão ausentes. Se você já tem um táxon em mente em vez de precisar de uma comparação com a FFB, mycobank_records()/spfungorum_records() recuperam diretamente tudo o que esses repositórios têm registrado sobre ele. Para submeter novos nomes ou correções à própria plataforma, consulte as diretrizes de contribuição em floradobrasil.jbrj.gov.br/consulta ou entre em contato com a equipe de coordenação da FFB pelo e-mail floraefungadobrasil@jbrj.gov.br.

title: Resolver sua própria lista de nomes de espécies
text: Aqui apresentamos um guia prático para as funções funga_search() e funga_match() do pacote fungaR. Diferente de funga_records(), que navega pela própria lista de espécies, essas duas funções recebem uma lista de nomes que você já possui — de um herbário próprio, levantamento de campo ou colaborador — e a resolvem em relação à lista de espécies da Flora e Funga do Brasil (FFB).
crumbs: Resolver sua própria lista de nomes de espécies

title: Resolver sua própria lista de nomes de espécies
section: funga_search(): resolver uma única lista de nomes
text:
funga_search(): resolver uma única lista de nomes
A funga_search() compara cada nome de um vetor de caracteres com a lista de espécies da FFB. Ela tenta uma correspondência exata primeiro; se nenhuma for encontrada, recorre a uma correspondência aproximada (distância de Levenshtein generalizada), que é o que captura erros de digitação e pequenas variações ortográficas. Quando várias entradas da lista de espécies poderiam corresponder, a classificada como "NOME_ACEITO" (aceito) é preferida, de modo que sinônimos são automaticamente resolvidos para seu nome aceito.

Argumentos







Argumento
Descrição




splist
Vetor de caracteres com os nomes fúngicos a buscar.


version
Versão do conjunto de dados da FFB a usar. Padrão "latest".


max_distance
Distância de edição máxima permitida para uma correspondência aproximada — um número inteiro de edições, ou uma fração do tamanho do nome (ex.: 0.2 permite aproximadamente 1 edição a cada 5 caracteres). Padrão 0.2.


show_correct
Se TRUE, adiciona uma coluna Correct sinalizando correspondências exatas (TRUE) vs. aproximadas (FALSE).


genus_fuzzy
Se FALSE (padrão), o gênero deve corresponder exatamente e apenas o epíteto é comparado de forma aproximada — consideravelmente mais rápido para listas grandes.


progress_bar
Se TRUE, exibe uma barra de progresso.


rm_funga_database
Se TRUE, exclui o banco de dados em cache após a busca. O padrão FALSE é recomendado para uso repetido.





Exemplos
library(fungaR)

# Um único nome aceito
funga_search("Trichoderma harzianum")

# Um epíteto com erro de digitação, sinalizando correspondências exatas vs. aproximadas
funga_search("Trichoderma harzianun", max_distance = 0.2, show_correct = TRUE)

# Um sinônimo - resolve automaticamente para o nome aceito
funga_search("Xylaria cornuta")

# Uma lista inteira de uma só vez
splist <- c("Trichoderma harzianum", "Xylaria polymorpha", "Trichoderma viride")
funga_search(splist, show_correct = TRUE, progress_bar = TRUE)

title: Resolver sua própria lista de nomes de espécies
section: funga_match(): comparar duas listas de nomes independentes
text:
funga_match(): comparar duas listas de nomes independentes
A funga_match() busca duas listas de nomes independentemente com funga_search(), e então alinha as entradas de ambas as listas que resolvem para o mesmo táxon aceito — mesmo quando um ou ambos os lados usaram um sinônimo. É útil para comparar sua lista de espécies com a de um colaborador, ou reconciliar dois conjuntos de dados que usaram nomenclaturas diferentes.

Argumentos







Argumento
Descrição




splist1, splist2
Vetores de caracteres — a lista de referência e a lista a comparar com ela.


include_all
Se TRUE (padrão), nomes encontrados apenas em splist2 são adicionados ao resultado.


identify_dups
Se TRUE (padrão), sinaliza linhas em que dois nomes de entrada são sinônimos do mesmo táxon aceito.


show_correct, genus_fuzzy, max_distance, version, rm_funga_database, progress_bar
Mesmo significado que em funga_search().





Exemplo
splist1 <- c("Trichoderma harzianum", "Xylaria polymorpha", "Trichoderma viride")
splist2 <- c("Xylaria polymorpha var. minor", "Trichoderma viride", "Xylaria cornuta")

result <- funga_match(splist1, splist2, include_all = TRUE)

# Reordenar splist2 para alinhar com splist1
splist2[result$Match.Position.2to1]

Dicas Adicionais

Mantenha rm_funga_database = FALSE (o padrão) ao longo de uma sessão: a primeira chamada de funga_search()/funga_match() baixa e analisa o conjunto de dados da FFB, e cada chamada seguinte reutiliza esse cache — buscas repetidas se tornam quase instantâneas.
Use show_correct = TRUE ao auditar uma lista de nomes, para que você possa revisar manualmente cada correspondência aproximada em vez de confiar nela cegamente.
A coluna Duplicated.Output.Position de funga_match() é útil para identificar quando dois dos seus próprios nomes acabam sendo sinônimos um do outro.

title: Encontrar espécies e registros estaduais ausentes na FFB
text:
Aqui apresentamos um guia prático para as funções mycobank_gap(), spfungorum_gap() e funga_distribution_gap() do pacote fungaR. Juntas, elas apoiam especialistas taxonomistas na curadoria e ampliação da cobertura fúngica da Flora e Funga do Brasil (FFB), cruzando dados com repositórios micológicos e de biodiversidade globais e sinalizando candidatos que merecem revisão manual.
Procurando informações do MycoBank ou do Index Fungorum sobre um táxon que você já tem em mente, em vez de uma comparação com a FFB? Veja Recuperar registros de um táxon brasileiro para mycobank_records()/spfungorum_records().
As três funções gravam seus resultados em três formas complementares: o data.frame retornado, uma planilha .xlsx para download e — por padrão (html_report = TRUE) — um relatório HTML autocontido com contagens-chave (KPIs), tabelas de resumo, e a tabela completa de candidatos/registros como um widget DT ordenável e filtrável, com botões de um clique para copiar ou baixar em CSV/Excel, aberto automaticamente no navegador em sessões interativas (open_report = interactive()).
